title: Lemon Cordial
subtitle: Sharp, fresh, clean lemon cordial, better than any bottle
excerpt: Lemon cordial is made with fresh lemon juice and zest in a sugar syrup. No cooking, the heat is just enough to dissolve the sugar. Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge. Makes about 1 litre.
sourceNotes: Classic British summer drink. Fresh lemon juice and zest give a brightness that bottled concentrate cannot replicate.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in ice cube trays for up to 6 months.

content.text: Homemade lemon cordial has a brightness and freshness that commercial versions simply don't match,  the zest adds a fragrance that juice alone can't provide. The method is simple: dissolve sugar in water, add lemon juice and zest, strain, and bottle. Makes about 1 litre of concentrated cordial.

items.prepNote: freshly squeezed, from about 8 to 10 lemons
optional, sharpens and extends shelf life

content.text: Put the sugar and water in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves completely. Remove from the heat as soon as it reaches a gentle simmer,  do not boil hard.
Stir in the lemon juice, zest, and citric acid if using. Leave to steep for 30 minutes to allow the zest to infuse. Strain through a fine sieve into sterilised bottles and seal.

items.cause: High sugar ratio, normal for a concentrate.
items.fix: Adjust the dilution ratio, try 1:10 with water or sparkling water. Alternatively, reduce sugar to 500 g next batch.

items.cause: Pith included when zesting, or juice from old lemons.
items.fix: Zest only the yellow outer skin, the white pith is bitter. Use freshly squeezed juice from unwaxed lemons.

items.cause: Not enough zest, or lemons with thin peel.
items.fix: Increase to 6 lemons for zest. Zest contributes more flavour than juice alone.

items.symptom: Cordial has gone cloudy and separated
items.fix: Shake before using. This is aesthetic only; the flavour is fine.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 3 weeks. Freeze for up to 6 months.
